title: Fragmented micro-session sandbox: deferred synthesis & soft-checkpoints
body:
Context / problem statement:

We keep getting requests from mobile/web teams to make conversational features cheaper and snappier. Users frequently perform extremely short interactions (1-3 turns) interleaved with long idle times. Current session model pins a full tokenized prefix and forces the server to carry full KV caches or fall back to costly re-encoding.

Idea (very rough): split a long-lived conversation into many small "micro-sessions" (microsegments) with lightweight soft-checkpoints. Each micro-session holds compressed summary tokens + a tiny continuation hint. The runtime can choose to:
  - serve from an in-memory mini-KV (fast path) if the micro-session is warm, or
  - rehydrate from soft-checkpoint (cheap decode + partial KV rebuild), or
  - fall back to full context restore (expensive).

Key goals:
  - reduce average per-turn token cost for high volume short-turn workloads by 20–50%
  - keep median latency same or slightly improved for warm micro-sessions
  - graceful degradation: when full history is unavailable, return a best-effort synthesized continuation with explicit provenance.

User stories (prioritized):
  1) As a product engineer, I want cheap short replies for micro-interactions so I can enable threaded quick replies in the mobile app without exploding costs.
  2) As an SRE, I want deterministic bounds on memory per active user so we can capacity plan for peak mobile events.
  3) As a privacy officer, I want checkpoints to be redactable and encrypted by default.

Design thoughts / primitives:

1) Soft-checkpoint format (proto sketch):
  - compressed_summary: ~150 token compressed summary (semantic compression vector + short natural language summary)
  - resume_hint: up to 80 tokens of prioritized recent context (explicit turn list or token slice)
  - quality_vector: small fingerprint of generation/acceptance signals (temperature, heuristic score)
  - schema_version: v0.2

2) Micro-session lifecycle states:
  - warm: KV cached, low-latency, normal generation
  - cold: no KV cached, but soft-checkpoint available -> rehydrate path (fast resume)
  - orphaned: neither KV nor checkpoint -> synthesize fallback or require full restore

3) API surface (sketch):
  POST /v1/micro_sessions.start -> returns micro_session_id, checkpoint_hint
  POST /v1/micro_sessions.append -> attach new turn; runtime may decide to checkpoint
  POST /v1/micro_sessions.resume -> accept micro_session_id + resume_policy (fast|accurate|cheap)
  POST /v1/generate -> standard generation with optional micro_session_id header

Resume policies: cheap -> prefer summary + short resume_hint (saves tokens); accurate -> prefer full restore if within budget; fast -> aggressively use KV if warm else cheap

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
  - end-to-end: mobile app can start and resume a micro-session with no UX-visible artifacts
  - cost: mean tokens used per short-turn (<= 10 user tokens) reduced >=20% in cheap mode vs baseline
  - latency: P50 roundtrip generation not worse than baseline for warm sessions
  - security: checkpoint payloads encrypted at rest and scrubbed of PII in summary generation

Experiment matrix (quick plan):
  - cohort A (baseline): current session handling
  - cohort B (cheap resume): resume_policy=cheap
  - cohort C (accurate resume): resume_policy=accurate

Metrics to capture:
  - tokens_per_turn (user+model) by session length bucket
  - rehydrate_rate (how often we need full restore)
  - warm_cache_hit_rate
  - synthesized_fallback_rate and user engagement after fallback
  - memory_per_active_user at peak

Open questions / risks:
  - How much semantic compression quality do we lose for multi-turn coherence? need micro-eval.
  - Pricing model implications: if we add a new resume type, how do we bill tokens vs resume-cost? (bill for tokens generated + resume overhead estimate?)
  - Compliance: summarized checkpoint may itself be sensitive. Must provide opt-out and enterprise controls to disable checkpointing.
  - Multi-device concurrency: if user interacts from two devices, merging micro-sessions could be tricky. Need merge policy (last-write wins vs operational transform?).

Prototype roadmap (6 weeks):
  Week 0–1: lightweight server-side prototype storing soft-checkpoints in Redis + proof-of-concept compression (distil-summarizer model)
  Week 2: integrate resume_policy param and instrument metrics
  Week 3: mobile client changes (SDK v0.8): keep micro_session_id cached and send resume hints
  Week 4: run small A/B with internal beta (10k users) comparing cost & latency
  Week 5: collect micro-evals for coherence regressions and tune compression thresholds
  Week 6: iterate on security redaction flow & enterprise opt-out

Operational knobs we should expose in Console:
  - checkpoint_frequency (turns or time)
  - max_resume_hint_tokens
  - resume_policy default per-customer
  - retention_period for checkpoints

Notes to self (random):
  - try a tiny VQVAE-style token compressor vs simple abstractive summarizer; maybe cheaper to store vector and rehydrate with short decode.
  - consider a "probe" request that warms KV with a single cheap token for long-idle sessions (warmup heuristic)
  - link up with billing to ensure visibility into micro-session savings (Metric: tokens_saved_estimate)

Quick mock example (client flow):
  1) User taps quick-reply -> client calls micro_sessions.start (intent: quick-turn)
  2) Server returns micro_session_id + checkpoint_hint
  3) Client posts user text with micro_session_id -> server appends and responds quickly (cheap path)
  4) After a few turns server decides to checkpoint (on-device idle or explicit save)
  5) Later resume: client calls micro_sessions.resume with policy=cheap -> server uses summary+resume_hint to reconstruct partial KV and continue

Potential KPIs for product:
  - average cost per active DAU for messaging product
  - % of mobile interactions served from warm or cheap resume paths
  - user satisfaction delta when fallback occurs (NPS sketch)

Immediate next steps (today/tomorrow):
  - sync with Maya (applied-ml) on candidate summarizer models (INF-9876)
  - quick spike to store & read a 230-byte soft-checkpoint from Redis
  - write a simple micro-eval: keep core conversation, remove checkpoint, and compute coherence score (ROUGE / embed-sim)

Random parking-lot ideas (low priority):
  - deterministic micro-session ids derived from user-device fingerprint so we can cheaply route requests to sticky pools
  - hybrid billing: small fixed resume fee + token billing for generations
  - UI hint: show a small "Resuming…" shimmer when accurate resume is in progress so user understands delay

---

Notes: this is exploratory. Lots of unknowns. Need to keep costs of added complexity smaller than token savings. Write down demo flow for next demo day (end of month).
